rule: How each career travels for a student who hopes to work abroad (owner, Round 13). travels_well: skills recognised widely, the hurdles are the visa and the job. requalify: a licensed profession — the destination's licence or registration comes first. india_based: runs through Indian state institutions. Licence rows are shown only when supported by the licensing body's own site (url) and published guidance; draft rows stay hidden. Never pay or demand figures abroad; never used in ranking.

recognition.name: Government of Canada — getting your credentials recognised
CareerOneStop (US Department of Labor) — licences by state
UK ENIC — recognition of overseas qualifications
Department of Home Affairs — skills assessment

countries_source.note: The top five destinations for Indian students, from the Ministry of External Affairs' data on Indian students abroad tabled in Parliament (2025)

review.note: Licence rows were checked against published guidance and point at each licensing body's own site; the official pages themselves could not be opened from the build container. The study bot re-checks them every January on those domains.

US.steps: ECFMG certification, then a US residency (Match), then a state licence

CA.steps: Credentials checked, MCCQE, then a residency or practice-ready assessment in a province

UK.steps: English test (IELTS/OET), PLAB 1, PLAB 2 in the UK, then GMC registration

AU.body: Australian Medical Council / Medical Board of Australia
AU.steps: AMC exams (or a competent-authority route), then registration through AHPRA

DE.steps: German to C1 for medicine, the medical language exam, usually the knowledge exam, then Approbation

US.body: Joint Commission on National Dental Examinations / state board
US.steps: Usually a 2–3 year advanced-standing DDS/DMD at a US school, the INBDE, then a state licence

CA.body: National Dental Examining Board of Canada
CA.steps: The NDEB equivalency exams (or a qualifying degree), then a provincial licence

UK.steps: English test, ORE Part 1 and Part 2, then GDC registration

AU.steps: ADC assessment and exams, then registration with the Dental Board through AHPRA

DE.steps: German for dentistry, the language exam, usually the knowledge exam, then Approbation

US.steps: English test, credentials evaluation, NCLEX-RN, then a state licence

CA.body: National Nursing Assessment Service / provincial college
CA.steps: NNAS assessment, the provincial college's review, NCLEX-RN, then registration

UK.steps: English test (IELTS/OET), the CBT (can be taken in India), the OSCE in the UK, then NMC registration

AU.body: Nursing and Midwifery Board of Australia (AHPRA)
AU.steps: English test, the NMBA assessment, then registration through AHPRA

DE.steps: German to B2, recognition of the qualification, usually an exam or adaptation period, then the licence

US.steps: FPGEC certification (FPGEE + English), internship hours, NAPLEX and the state law exam

CA.steps: Document evaluation, the PEBC exams, then a provincial licence

UK.steps: The one-year OSPAP course, a foundation year, the GPhC assessment, then registration

AU.steps: APC assessment and KAPS, supervised practice, then registration through AHPRA

DE.steps: German to B2–C1, recognition, usually the knowledge exam, then Approbation

US.steps: FCCPT credentials review, the NPTE, then a state licence (US entry level is a doctorate, so extra study is common)

CA.steps: CAPR credentialling, the PCE, then a provincial licence

UK.steps: English test, the HCPC's review of your training, then registration

AU.steps: APC assessment and exams, then registration through AHPRA

DE.steps: German to B2, recognition of the training, then the protected title Physiotherapeut

US.steps: Educational equivalence certification, the NAVLE, then a state licence

CA.steps: The NEB certification, then a provincial licence

UK.steps: English test, the statutory exam, then RCVS membership

AU.steps: AVBC assessment and the AVE, then registration with a state board

DE.steps: German, recognition, usually the knowledge exam, then Approbation

US.steps: A doctorate judged equivalent, supervised hours, the EPPP, then a state licence

CA.steps: Each province decides; most ask for a doctorate, supervised practice and the EPPP

UK.steps: The HCPC's review of your training, sometimes a test of competence, then registration

AU.steps: Qualification assessment, often supervised practice, then registration

DE.steps: A long German route; check the recognition finder

US.body: New York State Board of Law Examiners (and other states)
US.steps: An LLM at a US school, then the bar exam in a state such as New York

CA.body: Federation of Law Societies — National Committee on Accreditation
CA.exam: NCA challenge exams, then the provincial bar
CA.steps: NCA assessment and exams, then articling and the provincial licensing exams

UK.steps: The SQE (Indian lawyers may get exemptions), then admission as a solicitor

AU.body: State admission board (e.g. LPAB New South Wales)
AU.steps: The board assesses your degree and names subjects to complete, then admission

DE.steps: Recognition; if your training differs a lot, an aptitude test in German law

US.steps: No direct route from the Indian CA yet: credentials evaluation, then the CPA exam

CA.exam: CPA route for internationally trained accountants
CA.steps: ICAI has an MOU with CPA Canada; the provincial CPA body sets what remains

UK.steps: ICAI has an MOU with ICAEW; the remaining exams depend on the route

AU.exam: Mutual recognition (one paper for CPA Australia)
AU.steps: ICAI has mutual recognition with CA ANZ and CPA Australia

DE.steps: German titles need their own exams in German

US.exam: EESA review, AXP and the ARE
US.steps: Education evaluated (EESA), experience logged (AXP), the ARE exams, then a state licence

CA.steps: Education certified by CACB (or BEFA for experienced architects), then a provincial association

UK.steps: The ARB exam for overseas qualifications, then registration

AU.exam: Overseas qualifications assessment or experienced-practitioner route
AU.steps: AACA assessment, then registration with a state board

DE.exam: Recognition + entry in the list of architects
DE.steps: Recognition of the degree, usually two years' experience, then entry in the chamber's list

US.steps: An FAA licence on the basis of your DGCA licence, then the full commercial licence and type rating

CA.steps: Transport Canada's conversion of a foreign ICAO licence

UK.exam: UK ATPL theory and skill test
UK.steps: UK CAA licence: the theory exams, then a skill test

AU.steps: CASA converts ICAO licences after exams and a flight test

DE.steps: An EASA licence: the ATPL theory, then a skill test

US.steps: Each state certifies teachers; credentials evaluation and state tests

CA.body: Provincial teacher regulator (e.g. Ontario College of Teachers)
CA.steps: Each province certifies teachers; Ontario's college is one example

UK.steps: Apply for QTS if you trained as a teacher outside the UK

AU.body: AITSL and the state teacher registration board
AU.steps: Qualification assessment, then registration in the state you teach in

DE.steps: German states recognise teachers separately, usually needing two subjects and German
